newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Amcor sees improvement later in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Amcor sees improvement later in 96/97.

text.p: Paper and packaging group Amcor Ltd said on Monday it expected to see some signs of improved trading conditions later in the 1996/97 year ending June 30.

"The difficult conditions experienced in January-June 1996 have continued into the new financial year, but there are signs of an improvement later in the year," the company said in a statement accompanying its annual results.

"Paper prices, for example, appear to have bottomed, all Amcor businesses have restructuring and cost reduction programmes underway and there are new busienss opportunities in all regions," Amcor said.
Earlier, Amcor posted a lower net profit of A$338.8 million, from A$359.7 million in 1994/95, and a 15.6 percent drop in pre-tax operating profit to A$519.7 million.
It kept its final dividend unchanged at 20 cents.
Amcor said the later half of the year to June had seen extreme changes in paper and other raw materials prices.

"A combination of unrelenting pressure on margins in the Australian and New Zealand packaging businesses and the lower overall level of business activity in Australia added up to a very difficult trading environment for all Amcor's businesses," Amcor said.
It said its paper group achieved excellent results in the first half of 1995/96, but the very rapid fall in paper prices during the second hit the group hard.

"While a high level of pulp self-sufficiency largely insulated APG (the paper group) from movements in world pulp prices, major international movements in paper prices are now quickly felt in Australia," it said.
"The sudden slide in prices for all paper grades in January-June 1996 had a severe impact on APG and on Amcor Merchanting and Trading."
Pre tax and interest profit from the paper group and the merchanting and trading divisions fell to A$262.7 million from A$271.4 million in 1994/95.
Analysts had forecast pre-abnormal net profits of about A$372 million for the year, compared with the A$356 million actually registered for 1995/96 and the A$402.6 million posted in 1994/95.
Earnings per share fell to 57.5 cents from 67.0 cents.
Amcor's containers packaging division posted a pre-tax and interest profit of A$235 million, down from A$239.5 million the previous year.
"Containers' results were adversely affected by unstable raw material prices and the sale of the profitable, but non-core, greeting cards and security printing businesses," Amcor said.
"Amcor Fibre Packaging earned lower profit before interest and tax, which reflected a highly competitive Australian market with margins under intense pressure as capacity exceeded demand," it said.
"Volumes in Australia, New Zealand and Germany were also affected by adverse economic conditions."
Amcor's shares were steady at A$7.74 at 10.15 a.m. (0015 GMT). -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
